messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to help calculate the slope gradient, but I’ll need the elevation (height above sea level) for each of the two points. With just latitude and longitude, I can compute the horizontal distance between them, but the slope gradient also depends on how much the terrain rises or falls between those points.

Could you provide the elevation values for:

1. (40.7128, –74.0060)  
2. (34.0522, –118.2437)

Once I have those, I can compute the slope gradient in degrees for you.
message.reasoning: We need to calculate slope gradient between two points. But slope gradient between two points on a landscape? Usually slope gradient requires elevation difference and horizontal distance. We only have coordinates (latitude, longitude). No elevation. So we cannot compute slope gradient. We can compute great-circle distance between points. But slope gradient requires elevation difference. So we need to ask for elevation data. Or we can explain that we need elevation. So respond accordingly.
